title: Skull-melt Czochralski: quartz-free silicon in a cold copper crucible
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero quartz crucibles. Melt silicon in a water-cooled, segmented copper crucible where the induction field both heats and pushes the melt off the wall, so a frozen silicon 'skull' is the only contact surface; pull 300 mm ingots from that pool and use nitrogen co-doping to replace the wafer-strengthening role of crucible-derived oxygen.
why: Removes the Spruce Pine >80% HPQ chokepoint for every DRAM wafer; the skull is reused indefinitely, so crucible cost (~$1-3k per pull) goes to ~0 and oxygen-precipitate variability disappears; the cost is higher RF power per kg.

title: Synthetic crucibles from polysilicon-plant tetrachloride waste
idea: Imposed scarcity: no natural high-purity quartz. Take the SiCl4 byproduct that Siemens polysilicon plants make (~3-4 kg per kg of poly), flame-hydrolyze it into silica soot as optical-fiber preform makers do, and press and sinter the soot into whole crucibles (not just inner liners) next to U.S. poly plants.
why: Turns a waste stream into a domestic HPQ substitute and decouples crucibles from one North Carolina deposit; low-alkali synthetic silica can raise crucible life and ingot yield ~10-20%.

title: Ion-cut prime silicon films onto cast metallurgical carriers
idea: Imposed scarcity: one CZ wafer must feed ten DRAM wafers. Hydrogen-implant and split a 1.5 um prime silicon layer from a reusable CZ donor, bond it over a thin oxide-nitride diffusion barrier onto a cheap cast upgraded-metallurgical silicon carrier (made in graphite or Si3N4 molds), and build the array in the transferred film.
why: ~10x less CZ crystal and HPQ crucible per wafer; the carrier costs ~$5-10 vs ~$100+ for prime 300 mm; the buried barrier can also serve as a back-bias plane for leakage control.

title: Molten-salt electro-epitaxy grows wafers without Siemens or Czochralski
idea: Imposed scarcity: no polysilicon reactor and no crystal puller. Electrodeposit 300-700 um of single-crystal silicon from a KF-KCl-K2SiF6 molten salt at ~750 C onto a seed wafer capped with a weak porous-silicon release layer, then peel off the grown wafer and reuse the seed.
why: Collapses polysilicon (Siemens ~60-100 kWh/kg) and CZ (HPQ crucible, argon) into one low-temperature electrochemical step; a possible ~3x energy cut per wafer and zero crucible use.

title: Thin-kerf, thin-wafer diet: more wafers per crucible
idea: Imposed scarcity: ingot output frozen at today's crucible count. Slice 300 mm ingots with 35 um diamond wire into 450 um wafers (vs 775 um wafers with ~150 um kerf), and carry each thin wafer through FEOL on a reusable bonded glass or silicon handle that is debonded before backgrind.
why: Ingot consumed per wafer drops from ~925 um to ~490 um, so ~1.8x more wafers per ingot; the same Spruce Pine crucible and polysilicon supply feeds ~60-80% more DRAM wafers.

title: Barrierless molybdenum buried wordline from Colorado ore
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero tungsten (China ~80%). Fill the buried wordline trench by MoO2Cl2/H2 CVD of molybdenum directly on the work-function liner, dropping the TiN barrier because Mo needs no protection from fluorine, and source the precursor from U.S. Climax/Henderson molybdenum.
why: Removes WF6 and fluorine gate damage; Mo's short electron mean free path gives ~20-40% lower line resistance below 15 nm and reclaims ~2 nm of trench for metal; the supply is domestic.

title: Fully silicided nickel wordlines replace tungsten fill
idea: Imposed scarcity: no W and no WF6. Fill the wordline trench with doped amorphous silicon, cap it with Ni(Pt) and anneal so the whole trench converts to NiSi (full silicidation); the work function is tuned by dopant pile-up at the gate interface.
why: Removes tungsten and fluorine from the cell; work-function engineering by dopant segregation can cut GIDL and so the leakage tail that forces refresh; NiSi at ~15 uOhm-cm competes with narrow W lines.

title: Self-barrier copper-manganese bitlines from Arizona copper
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero tungsten and zero TiN on the bitline. Deposit a Cu-0.5%Mn alloy into the bitline trench; on anneal the Mn migrates to the dielectric and forms a ~1-2 nm MnSiOx self-barrier, so nearly the whole cross-section is copper.
why: Copper (~1.7 uOhm-cm bulk vs W ~5.6) lets bitlines run longer with fewer sense amps, attacking the 49% periphery share, while dropping a China-concentrated metal.

title: Catalytic wet-etched silicon molds for 115:1 capacitors
idea: Imposed scarcity: no fluorocarbon plasma and no high-aspect-ratio etch tool. Deposit a sacrificial silicon mold above a nitride barrier, pattern a graphene or Pt catalyst mesh, and let catalyst-assisted chemical etching in HF/H2O2 sink vertical holes beyond 100:1; line them with TiN/ZAZ, then dissolve the silicon mold in TMAH.
why: Reaches the AR~115 capacitor charge wall with no PFC gases (high GWP, PFAS rules) and no $5M+ etcher; holes stay straight because the catalyst sinks chemically rather than relying on ion flux.

title: Self-ordering anodic alumina pores as lithography-free capacitor molds
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero EUV and zero plasma for the capacitor layer. Deposit thick aluminum over the storage-node contacts, nanoimprint shallow pits on the contact grid, and anodize in sulfuric or oxalic acid so pores self-organize at the pits and grow straight to AR >100; open the barrier oxide at the bottom and fill with electrode and dielectric.
why: Replaces 1-2 EUV or multipatterning masks and the hardest dry etch with a room-temperature electrochemical step using abundant aluminum; capacitor AR is set only by film thickness.

title: Oxygen-ashable carbon mold capacitors with no HF dip-out
idea: Imposed scarcity: no fluorocarbon gases and no HF. Build the capacitor mold from amorphous carbon etched in O2/N2/COS plasma, deposit TiN/ZAZ at <=400 C, then remove the mold by O2 ashing instead of an HF wet dip-out.
why: Removes PFC etch gases and the wet capillary forces that topple tall pillars, so AR can rise from ~70 toward ~100 for more Cs; also cuts PFAS-regulated chemistry and UPW per wafer.

title: Rutile titania on MoO2 electrodes: hafnium- and zirconium-free capacitors
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero Zr and Hf. Use conductive MoO2 (a distorted-rutile oxide) as the storage-node electrode so ALD TiO2 grows directly as rutile (k ~80-100) at low temperature, with Al doping to hold down leakage in the thin film.
why: k~90 vs ZAZ ~40 lets the cell reach 5 fF at roughly half the aspect ratio, easing etch and leaning; uses abundant Ti and domestic Mo instead of nuclear-chain Zr/Hf precursors or PGM Ru electrodes.

title: Indium- and gallium-free zinc-tin-oxide gain cells
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero indium and gallium (China-dominated). Build a 2T0C gain cell whose write transistor is amorphous Zn-Sn-O made by ALD below 300 C, Si-doped to suppress oxygen-vacancy leakage, with charge stored on the read transistor's gate.
why: Off-current near 1e-19 A/um stretches retention from 64 ms to minutes, removing most of the ~46 fJ/bit refresh; uses earth-abundant Zn and little Sn instead of IGZO's critical metals.

title: Supercritical CO2 replaces ultrapure water in cleaning
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero ultrapure water for post-etch clean and dry. Run residue removal and drying in supercritical CO2 with small co-solvent and chelator doses inside sealed cluster modules, recompressing and recycling >95% of the CO2.
why: UPW use (~2-4 m3 per wafer) can fall up to ~50%; with no liquid meniscus tall capacitor pillars do not collapse, which allows higher AR; fabs in water-stressed U.S. sites become permittable.

title: Fiber-drawn salami capacitor arrays sliced into wafers
idea: Imposed scarcity: no lithography and no high-AR etch. Assemble a glass preform of millimetre metal-cored, glass-clad coaxial rods, thermally draw and restack-redraw it (as photonic-crystal fiber makers do) until cores reach ~50 nm pitch, then slice the fused bundle into 5 um discs and hybrid-bond them to a CMOS access-transistor wafer.
why: Feature size comes from draw ratio, not EUV; each slice is a sheet of billions of coaxial capacitors with AR ~100 at no etch cost, made from glass and common metals.

title: Silicon-free DRAM on glass panels in idled display fabs
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero silicon wafers. Make 1T1C memory with oxide-TFT access transistors and stacked MIM capacitors on Gen-8.5 glass panels in under-used display fabs, stacking 4-8 cell layers to offset the ~1 um design rule, and pair it with a small CMOS controller.
why: A 5.5 m2 panel has ~75x a 300 mm wafer's area and uses float glass instead of CZ silicon, HPQ crucibles or EUV; it targets a low-cost CXL far-memory tier rather than HBM.

title: LNG regasification cold runs refresh-free cryogenic memory racks
idea: Imposed scarcity: no power budget for refresh. Site memory-heavy data halls at LNG import terminals and use the ~-160 C cold released during regasification, through a nitrogen loop, to hold DRAM at ~100-120 K, where access-transistor leakage collapses and refresh intervals can stretch >1000x.
why: Refresh (16-33% of idle DRAM power) and most cooling energy disappear using free waste cold, with no helium; higher carrier mobility at low temperature also trims access time.

title: Brownfield DRAM fabs on retired coal plants
idea: Imposed scarcity: no new water rights, no new transmission and no greenfield permit time. Site fabs on retiring coal plants that already hold industrial water allocations, cooling reservoirs, high-voltage interconnects and rail, and convert boiler halls into utility buildings.
why: Fab water (~10-20 ML/day) and 100-300 MW of power are often the binding permits; reuse could cut 1-2 years and ~$1B in utilities from a U.S. fab schedule.

title: Hot-swap chamber liner cassettes eliminate NF3 in-situ cleans
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero NF3 or fluorinated chamber-clean gas. Build ALD/CVD chamber walls from robot-swappable liner cassettes; after N wafers, swap in a fresh cassette in minutes and strip the dirty one offline in a closed-loop alkaline electrochemical bath that recovers the TiN and ZrO2 deposits.
why: In-situ NF3 cleans are a top fab greenhouse emission and a fluorochemical dependency; this removes them, recovers Zr, and raises uptime because clean-and-season cycles vanish.

title: Molecular monolayer doping replaces arsine and phosphine implants
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero toxic hydride gases and no implanter for cell junctions. Graft a self-assembled monolayer of phosphorus- or boron-bearing molecules onto silicon, cap it with oxide and spike-anneal to drive a sub-5 nm conformal junction, which also works on the sidewalls of lateral 3D-DRAM channels that beamline implants cannot reach.
why: Removes concentrated AsH3/PH3/BF3 supply chains and ~$5-10M implanters per layer; conformal doping unblocks lateral transistors, a key 3D-DRAM blocker.

title: Hafnium-free periphery on mature SiON wafers bonded under array
idea: Imposed scarcity: no hafnium and no EUV in the periphery. Build sense amps, decoders and I/O on a separate 40 nm poly/SiON CMOS wafer in any mature U.S. fab and hybrid-bond it face-to-face under the array wafer.
why: Periphery is ~49% of the die; moving it to a Hf-free, EUV-free, depreciated node cuts EUV layers and scarce precursors per bit and frees array area for ~1.5-1.8x bits per array wafer.

title: Silicon-carbide furnace ware removes the second quartz dependency
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero HPQ anywhere in the fab, not just in crucibles. Replace quartz diffusion tubes, boats, injectors and bell jars with CVD-SiC-coated or recrystallized SiC, plus single-crystal silicon parts machined from ingot tops and tails.
why: Fab quartzware also depends on Spruce Pine-grade sand; SiC parts last ~3-5x longer at high temperature and survive HF cleans, cutting consumable volume and chokepoint exposure.

title: Ceria-free shallow-trench planarization by selective dry etch-back
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero rare-earth ceria slurry and no CMP water. Fill isolation trenches with flowable oxide, then planarize with a self-limiting, nitride-stopping remote-plasma etch-back under optical endpoint control instead of ceria-slurry CMP.
why: Ceria is a China-concentrated rare earth and CMP is a major slurry and UPW consumer; dry etch-back also reduces dishing and particle defects, removing one chokepoint per STI layer.

title: Decommissioned-server DIMM harvest into CXL memory sleds
idea: Within $1M/24 months: buy a used memory tester and handler (~$250k), purchase decommissioned DDR4 RDIMMs by the ton from hyperscaler IT-asset-disposition channels, burn in and rebin them, and sell them on off-the-shelf CXL Type-3 expander cards that take DDR4.
why: Every recycled GB is supply with zero new silicon, HPQ, W or He; at ~4x contract prices a 10 TB/month line pays back in months and relieves far-memory demand.

title: Post-package-repair rescue line for returned DIMMs
idea: Within $1M/24 months: write open firmware that runs exhaustive row-retention and hammer tests on returned and failing DDR4/DDR5 modules, then permanently remaps bad rows through JEDEC hard post-package-repair fuses and re-certifies modules that would otherwise be shredded.
why: A few failing rows now scrap whole modules; rescuing ~50-70% of returns adds supply with zero materials and yields field data on retention tails.

title: Point-of-use helium micro-recovery skid on tool exhaust
idea: Within $1M/24 months: build a refrigerator-sized skid that taps the foreline of He-backside etch and CVD tools, separates He from the N2 purge with a hollow-fiber membrane plus a small PSA stage, and returns 99.99% He to the chuck supply; pilot it on 3 tools.
why: Captures ~60-80% of per-tool helium while Qatar's ~30% is offline, with payback in months at shortage prices and no fab-wide liquefier.

title: Hydrogen backside cooling retrofit for etch chucks
idea: Within $1M/24 months: in a university fab, retrofit a used 300 mm etcher's electrostatic chuck to run H2 backside gas at ~10 Torr (no O2 present, so no ignition path), with Pd-getter cleanup and leak interlocks, and map wafer temperature against He.
why: H2's thermal conductivity (~0.18 W/m-K) exceeds He's (~0.15), so cooling is equal or better while removing the largest per-wafer helium use; H2 can be made anywhere.

title: Barium-armored crucibles from non-Spruce Pine quartz
idea: Within $1M/24 months: coat the inner wall of crucibles made from lower-grade Norwegian or U.S. quartz with a barium-hydroxide wash that nucleates a dense, uniform cristobalite skin at melt-in to act as an impurity diffusion barrier; validate on a 4-6 inch lab puller with lifetime and oxygen metrology.
why: If the skin blocks alkali and Al outdiffusion, crucibles no longer need Spruce Pine (>80%) HPQ; lab pullers make the test affordable within the budget.

title: Controlled-spalling wafer multiplication demo
idea: Within $1M/24 months: electroplate a stressed nickel layer on 300 mm prime wafers, start a crack to peel 20 um single-crystal films onto low-cost carriers, re-polish the parent and repeat ~20x; prove gate-oxide integrity and junction leakage on the spalled films.
why: Each CZ wafer (and its share of HPQ crucible and polysilicon) yields up to 20 device substrates; spalling is room-temperature and needs few tools, unlike ion-cut.

title: Diamond-wire kerf recycled into Czochralski recharge feedstock
idea: Within $1M/24 months: bench-pilot recovery of silicon kerf from 300 mm wafering (30-40% of the ingot) using froth flotation to strip coolant and diamond, an HCl leach for Fe/Ni, and induction melting with slag refining into recharge rods that meet CZ spec.
why: Returns about a third of every ingot to feedstock, cutting polysilicon demand and Siemens energy per wafer by up to ~30%.

title: Carbide-scrap tungsten turned into domestic WF6
idea: Within $1M/24 months: bench pilot that takes U.S. cemented-carbide scrap (drill bits, inserts) through the zinc reclaim process, oxidizes and hydrogen-reduces it to tungsten powder, fluorinates it with on-site F2, and distills 6N WF6 for wordline CVD.
why: Breaks the China ~80% primary-tungsten dependence for fab precursors using an existing domestic scrap stream; DRAM needs only tonnes, so a small plant covers a U.S. fab.

title: Cold-trap recovery of unreacted zirconium ALD precursors
idea: Within $1M/24 months: insert a temperature-staged cold trap between capacitor ALD chambers and their pumps to condense unreacted Zr/Hf amide precursors (often >90% of dosed mass), then fractionally distill and re-certify them; validate on one ZAZ tool.
why: Cuts Zr/Hf precursor purchases ~3-5x and abatement load, easing both precursor cost and nuclear-chain Hf/Zr supply.

title: MOF cartridges capture neon, krypton and xenon from exhaust
idea: Within $1M/24 months: package selective metal-organic-framework adsorbents (Xe/Kr-selective SBMOF-type beds plus a Ne-capture stage) into swappable cartridges on excimer-laser and etch exhausts, regenerate them offsite by temperature swing, and resell the rare gases.
why: Ne/Kr/Xe supply is tied to Russian and Ukrainian air-separation byproducts; cartridges target ~70-90% recovery for DUV lasers and etch at cartridge rather than plant capex.

title: Idle-RAM leasing agent across colocation tenants
idea: Within $1M/24 months: ship an open-source hypervisor agent that exposes each server's idle DRAM as encrypted RDMA-backed remote swap to neighboring tenants through a spot-price market, starting in one colo with 500 servers.
why: Typical clusters strand ~30-50% of installed DRAM; renting it out displaces new-DIMM purchases with zero new materials.

title: Defense Production Act priority rating for semiconductor helium
idea: Within $1M/24 months: fund analysis and a coalition petition for DPA Title I priority ratings (DO/DX) on U.S.-produced helium, NF3 and WF6 deliveries to domestic memory fabs during declared shortages, with a fab-usage reporting template.
why: Shortage allocation is now first-come or contract-based; rated-order priority keeps U.S. DRAM lines running at negligible public cost.

title: Fab consortium pre-buys helium from small U.S. wells
idea: Within $1M/24 months: form a buyers' consortium that signs 10-year forward offtake with small helium developers in Kansas, Montana and Wyoming, using the $1M for diligence, legal setup and escrow seed while member fabs supply the volume commitment.
why: Small helium projects stall for lack of offtake; guaranteed demand unlocks new domestic supply and removes Qatar exposure.

title: Scribe-line sensors replace blanket monitor wafers
idea: Within $1M/24 months: put film-thickness, sheet-resistance and particle test structures in product scribe lines and pair them with tool-sensor virtual-metrology models, so process qualification uses product wafers instead of blanket monitor wafers; pilot with one fab partner.
why: Monitor and dummy wafers consume ~10-20% of prime-wafer starts; halving them frees silicon, crucibles and helium for real DRAM.

title: Acoustic and infrared watch lets crucibles survive extra pulls
idea: Within $1M/24 months: retrofit crystal pullers with acoustic-emission sensors and IR wall imaging that detect bubble growth and cristobalite spalling in the quartz crucible, so operators safely add one more recharge pull per crucible instead of retiring it on a fixed schedule.
why: One extra pull per crucible means ~20-50% fewer crucibles per kg of ingot, directly stretching Spruce Pine supply.

title: Water-developable chitosan photoresist with zero PFAS
idea: Within $1M/24 months: formulate a chitosan- or cellulose-derived resist with non-fluorinated sulfonium photoacid generators that develops in plain water, and characterize resolution and line-edge roughness on a university e-beam writer and 248 nm scanner.
why: PFAS photoacid generators and solvents face EU and U.S. restrictions; a water-developed bio-resist removes both and cuts solvent waste.

title: Glass-lined, SiC-coated wet benches replace fluoropolymer plumbing
idea: Within $1M/24 months: build one acid wet-bench loop with borosilicate-glass-lined stainless piping, CVD-SiC tank linings and ceramic valve seats instead of PFA/PTFE, and qualify metal-ion leaching to ppt levels over 12 months.
why: Fabs depend on PFA/PTFE wetted parts that pending PFAS restrictions threaten; a proven fluoropolymer-free path de-risks every U.S. fab.

title: Diamond-electrode loop regenerates sulfuric acid resist strip
idea: Within $1M/24 months: put a boron-doped-diamond electrolysis cell on the SPM resist-strip bath to oxidize spent sulfuric acid into peroxydisulfuric acid in situ, removing H2O2 dosing and recycling the acid instead of draining it.
why: SPM strips use large acid and peroxide volumes; closed-loop regeneration cuts ~80-90% of those chemical purchases and the wastewater neutralization load.

title: Combinatorial abundant-element dielectric library for capacitors
idea: Within $1M/24 months: co-sputter graded Ti-Al-Si-Mg-Ca-O-N thin-film libraries (crustal-abundant elements only) on probe-array wafers, auto-measure k, leakage and breakdown across ~10,000 compositions, and hand the top 10 to ALD recipe development.
why: Searches for a k>=60, low-leakage capacitor dielectric with no Hf, Zr, Sr or rare earths, aimed straight at the capacitor charge wall, at lab cost.

title: Endpoint-sensed rinses replace fixed-time water rinses
idea: Within $1M/24 months: retrofit wet benches with inline resistivity and TOC sensors in the rinse drain and software that ends each rinse when effluent purity recovers, instead of fixed worst-case recipes; pilot on 10 benches.
why: Fixed-time rinses overspend UPW by ~20-40%; endpointing saves water and UPW-production energy per wafer with no process change.

title: Recover ceria from spent CMP slurry
idea: Within $1M/24 months: bench pilot that concentrates spent STI CMP slurry by ultrafiltration, dissolves silica fines in dilute caustic, recovers ceria by flocculation, and re-calcines it to abrasive spec for reuse.
why: Cuts purchases of China-concentrated rare-earth ceria by ~50-70% and reduces slurry waste, on existing CMP tools.

title: Assay campaign for second-source U.S. quartz pegmatites
idea: Within $1M/24 months: core and assay candidate pegmatites (Black Hills, Maine, Georgia) for low-Al/Ti/alkali quartz, run hot-chlorination and flotation purification trials, and make test crucible billets with partner crucible makers.
why: One qualified second U.S. HPQ source breaks the single-valley (>80%) chokepoint; the budget covers drilling and lab purification.

title: Million-dollar bounty for a chokepoint-free capacitor module
idea: Within $1M/24 months: put the whole budget into staged prizes ($100k milestones, $500k grand prize) for any team that shows a DRAM capacitor module of >=5 fF at <=40 nm pitch using no He, W, Hf/Zr, PFAS or HPQ-dependent steps, verified by an independent university fab.
why: Prizes often draw 10-40x their value in outside effort, turning a tiny budget into dozens of parallel material searches aimed at the capacitor charge wall.
